title: AI Receptionist vs Answering Service: What's Better for Tradies?
excerpt: Answering services cost $800/month and just take messages. Here's why a modern call handling system books more jobs for less.
author: Active FrontDesk
content:
## The problem with traditional answering services

Most answering services work like this: someone in a call centre picks up, takes a name and number, and emails you a message. Then you have to call the customer back.

By the time you call back — usually hours later — they've already booked someone else.

### What a modern call handling system does differently

Instead of just taking a message, a proper system:

1. **Answers in 2 rings** — no hold music, no "please wait"
2. **Has a natural conversation** — asks what the issue is, gets their details
3. **Books the appointment** — straight into your Google Calendar
4. **Sends an SMS confirmation** — the customer knows it's sorted
5. **Logs everything** — name, number, job details, all in your CRM

The customer hangs up with a confirmed booking. You check your calendar and the job's already there.

### Cost comparison

| | Answering Service | Call Handling System |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly cost | $800+ | $400 |
| Books appointments? | No — just takes messages | Yes — directly in your calendar |
| Available 24/7? | Usually business hours only | Yes — every call, every time |
| SMS confirmations? | No | Yes |
| CRM logging? | No | Yes |
| Call back required? | Yes — always | Only for complex jobs |

### The real difference: jobs booked vs messages taken

An answering service creates work for you — you still have to call everyone back. A call handling system eliminates that step entirely.

When a customer calls at 7pm on a Saturday about a blocked drain, they get a confirmed booking for Monday morning. Not a voicemail. Not a message that sits in your inbox until Tuesday.

### Which one pays for itself?

If your average job is $350, you need just over one extra booking per month to cover the cost. Most businesses see 5-10 additional bookings in their first month.
